fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`caused_by` auto-derivation falls back to best-effort `git blame` over a bug's impacted paths
when no `--caused-by` is supplied (`rebar.metrics.blame.derive_caused_by`, invoked from
`_commands/transition_close.py::_resolve_caused_by_culprit` only when the bug carries no
`caused_by` edge yet). The edge feeds `rebar metrics`' escape-rate lenses and the epic-close
`caused_by` floor, and a WRONG edge is worse than an absent one: it silently charges an escaped
defect to a ticket whose reviewers could not plausibly have caught it.

Whether the file-level auto-derivation is accurate for this codebase's dominant defect shapes is
an OPEN QUESTION with no direct evidence either way — see the two correction comments below: the
original "usually wrong" claim conflated hand-run line-level `git blame` with the file-level
auto-derivation, and the first retraction's counter-evidence ("blame ran on four closes and
agreed") was itself void because the `--caused-by` flag worked and blame never ran. The proven
part is only that the dominant defect shapes here (unmet obligations, carrier commits, omissions)
are structurally hard for blame. This ticket measures rather than asserts.

## Approach

Measure the actual mechanism (`derive_caused_by`) against the actual store, read-only:

1. **Enumerate the population.** Reduce every ticket in the tracker; select closed `bug` tickets
   whose reduced state carries at least one active `caused_by` edge. Report the population size.
2. **Re-run the real deriver on each.** For every sampled bug, call
   `rebar.metrics.blame.derive_caused_by(bug_id, repo_root, tracker)` in this worktree (full git
   history, current HEAD) and compare its output to the recorded edge target:
   agreement / disagreement / abstention (`None`). Because the recorded edge carries NO
   derived-vs-explicit marker (`_apply_caused_by` writes via `_write_link_event` with no
   provenance field — verified at src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py), this classification
   BOUNDS rather than identifies the blame-derived population, and the findings must say so:
   agreement means "consistent with blame-derivation" (a supplied edge can coincide with
   blame); disagreement/abstention means "not reproducible by the deriver TODAY", which is
   evidence of explicit supply but not proof — the deriver abstains or diverges for reasons
   unrelated to supply (the fixing commit no longer resolving, `file_impact` paths since
   renamed/deleted, the pre-fix blame no longer yielding a strict >50% majority after
   reformat/move carriers landed on top, or the culprit commit's trailer no longer resolving).
   Each non-agreement case is therefore annotated with the deriver's observable failure reason
   (no-fixing-commit / no-file-impact / no-majority / unresolvable-culprit / different-target),
   and the classification is reported as a bound with those caveats, never as a
   supplied-vs-derived truth.
3. **Score accuracy against proven origins.** For the subsample of bugs whose ticket record
   independently establishes the true origin (a root-cause comment or description naming the
   introducing ticket — the `/rebar-debug` protocol writes these), compare the deriver's output
   to that proven origin and classify each case: correct / wrong-target / abstained. Classify
   each wrong/abstained case by defect shape (unmet obligation / carrier commit / omission /
   other) so the rate connects to the shapes hypothesis.
4. **Record the two decisions** the measurement informs, with reasoning, as a findings comment:
   (a) should a blame-derived edge be distinguishable on read from a supplied one;
   (b) should the fallback decline to attribute for shapes it cannot get right.
   Any resulting schema change or review-time criterion is FILED as its own ticket linked
   `discovered_from` this one — gate/criterion changes are operator-adjudicated, so those
   tickets are proposals for the operator, not work performed here.

Default assumptions (stated so no executor question remains): the sample is the WHOLE
population of closed bugs with `caused_by` edges (no sampling bias); a proven origin exists
only where the ticket record names one explicitly (no inferring ground truth from blame
itself); history drift (a bug fixed before later rebases/moves) counts as a named limitation,
not an error, when the deriver abstains for lack of the fixing commit.

## Scope

No repository file changes: measurement scripts run ad-hoc in the worktree interpreter against
the store and git history; results, methodology, and decisions are recorded on this ticket.
Follow-up implementation work (schema marker, deriver behaviour change, review criterion) is
filed as separate tickets, not done here.

## Testing / Verification

The deliverable is a measurement, so verification is reproducibility of the numbers: the
findings comment must quote the exact probe commands/snippets run (a Python snippet importing
`rebar.metrics.blame.derive_caused_by` and `rebar.reducer.reduce_ticket`, executed with this
worktree's `.venv` interpreter against the live tracker and git history) together with their
raw counts, so any reader can re-run the same snippet and reproduce the
agreement/disagreement/abstention table. The proving command for each numeric claim is that
quoted snippet; the proving evidence for each decision is its recorded reasoning referencing
those numbers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [non-codebase] The rate is measured, not estimated: the population of closed bugs with
      `caused_by` edges is enumerated (size reported), the real `derive_caused_by` is re-run on
      each, and the agreement/disagreement/abstention counts are reported in a findings comment
      on this ticket, with the method stated — checked by reading the comment.
      provenance: environment=work-50e3 worktree venv against the live tracker and full git history at current origin/main; principal=RebarBotNava analysis agent; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the real `derive_caused_by` was executed (not simulated) on all 88 population bugs; the findings comment quotes the exact snippet and raw counts (88 / agree 38 / disagree 6 / abstain 44).
- [x] [non-codebase] For every bug in the subsample with an independently proven origin, the
      deriver's output is scored correct / wrong-target / abstained and classified by defect
      shape; the proportion of blame-derivable edges naming a defensibly wrong origin is
      reported with the subsample size — checked by reading the comment.
      provenance: environment=work-50e3 worktree venv, ground truth read from the ticket store's root-cause records (the original description table + 17c3's root-cause comment); principal=RebarBotNava analysis agent; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the deriver's real output on each of the 8 proven-origin bugs was compared to the recorded proof: correct 0 / wrong-target 1 / abstained 7, each classified by defect shape in the findings table.
- [x] [non-codebase] A decision is recorded on whether a blame-derived edge should be
      distinguishable from an explicitly supplied one on read, with reasoning — checked by
      reading the comment.
      provenance: environment=work-50e3 worktree, reasoning grounded in the measurement's own numbers; principal=RebarBotNava analysis agent; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=static-analysis — the decision (YES, add a derived-vs-explicit marker) follows from the verified absence of any provenance field at the `_write_link_event` call sites in src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py plus the measured unanswerable 38/6/44 bound; recorded in the findings comment.
- [x] [non-codebase] A decision is recorded on whether the fallback should decline to attribute
      for the shapes it cannot get right, rather than guessing, with reasoning — checked by
      reading the comment.
      provenance: environment=work-50e3 worktree, reasoning grounded in the measured abstention and error rates; principal=RebarBotNava analysis agent; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=static-analysis — the decision (keep fail-closed as-is; shape is not observable to the mechanism; discount via the provenance marker instead) is recorded in the findings comment with the 50% population abstention and 7/8 subsample abstention figures as evidence.
- [x] [non-codebase] Any proposed review-time criterion or schema change is filed as its own
      ticket linked `discovered_from` this one rather than implemented here — checked by the
      links on this ticket.
      provenance: environment=work-50e3 worktree against the live tracker; principal=RebarBotNava analysis agent; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — proposal ticket highborn-gabardine-dairycow (6536-367c-e358-424d, provenance marker on caused_by link events) was created and linked discovered_from this ticket; no schema or criterion change was implemented (operator-adjudicated).
